title: Indocyanine green to assess vascularity of ileal conduit anastomosis and regulate ureteral resection margins during pelvic exenteration for recurrent/persistent gynecological cancer. A pilot study
official: Indocyanine green to assess vascularity of ileal conduit anastomosis and regulate ureteral resection margins during pelvic exenteration for recurrent/persistent gynecological cancer. A pilot study
summary: Main objective: to assess the vascularity of ileal conduit UD in patients undergoing ICG perfusion-modulated resection of ureters undergoing ileal conduit
conditions: Patients with gynecological cancers undergoing pelvic exenteration
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥18 years, and < 75 years
2. Cervical/vulvar/vaginal/endometrial cancer recurrence/progression or persistence suitable for pelvic exenteration histologically confirmed
3. Estimated life expectancy of at least 4 weeks
4. Signed written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Hypersensitivity to indocyanine green, to sodium iodide or to iodine
2. Subjects who are employed by or otherwise dependent on the sponsor or the investigator may not be enrolled in the study
3. Patients affected by hyperthyroidism, or with autoimmune thyroid adenomas
4. Severe kidney failure (eGFR <30ml/min/1,73m2)
5. Patients undergoing only posterior pelvic exenteration
6. Patients undergoing ureterostomy
7. Patients who underwent previous ureteral surgery (open, endoscopic or minimally invasive)
8. Refusal to sign written informed consent
9. Any clinical condition, which in the opinion of the investigator, places the subject at risk, prevents the subject from fully participating in the trial procedures, or potentially impairs the quality of the trial data
10. Participation in a clinical study in which an investigational drug was administered within 30 days or 5 half-lives before the ICG administration, whichever is longer
